_readme: DRAFT Fotheringhay walk (status draft in content/walks.json: only shown with draft colours on). Made by Claude from public sources; everything cyan until the owner approves. Character art still to make.
title: The White Rose
subtitle: Fotheringhay Walk
welcome_text: [[c:A short mystery walk around a tiny village with a royal past: the birthplace of Richard III and the place where Mary, Queen of Scots, was executed.]]
start_text: [[c:Start at the Falcon Inn, near the church in the middle of the village.]]

coins.explain: [[c:You have a purse of 5 coins for the whole walk. Hints are free. Showing an answer costs coins.]]

layers.label: Mystery story
layers.description: [[c:The story and the puzzles. Switch it off for a history-only walk.]]

route.name: St Mary and All Saints Church
route.label: Church

story: [[c:Fotheringhay, July 1476. King Edward IV has come to rebury his father, Richard, Duke of York, in the great church here, with feasting and ceremony.]]
[[c:The family's silver-gilt white rose, carried at the head of the procession, has vanished from the church on the night before the burial.]]

[[c:Four people were near it: Will Hobbs, a mason working on the church; Joan Fairfax, the castle cook; Kit Ashby, a young page; and Master Lucas Venn, a wine merchant from London. Find the white rose before the King finds out.]]

start_page.title: Getting to the start
start_page.intro: [[c:The walk starts and finishes at the Falcon Inn, close to the church.]]
parking: [[c:Parking: please park considerately on the village streets, or ask at the pub. If you're driving, park first and then open the walk.]]
start_page.support: [[c:Support the village: have a drink or a meal at the Falcon before or after your walk. The walk takes about 45 minutes to 1 hour 15.]]

directions.heading: [[c:How to get here]]
directions.text: [[c:Tap a button to open Google Maps with directions from where you are now.]]

lengths.label: [[c:Short walk: around the village]]
lengths.description: [[c:The church, the college site, the bridge and the castle mound. Fotheringhay sits on a T-junction, so parts of this are walked twice.]]

lengths.label: [[c:Longer walk: the brook path]]
lengths.description: [[c:Starts with a loop north across the fields and along the brook before the village stops.]]

short:1-2: [[c:Walk along Main Street past the junction to the church, about 250 metres.]]
